findings.issue: low_stock uses strict less-than (qty < threshold) instead of the spec's <= comparison, so an item exactly at the threshold qty is not reported as low stock.
findings.evidence: SPEC.md: "`Ledger.low_stock(threshold)`: SKUs with `qty <= threshold`." | stock.py line 30: "return [i.sku for i in self.items.values() if i.qty < threshold]"

findings.issue: test_stock.py contains no test at all for low_stock(), so the operator bug (and any future regression) is not caught by the test suite; the only test present covers add/total_value_cents.
findings.fix: Add a test asserting that an item with qty == threshold is included in low_stock's result, plus a case for qty above/below threshold.
findings.evidence: SPEC.md: "`Ledger.low_stock(threshold)`: SKUs with `qty <= threshold`." | test_stock.py only defines test_add_and_total (lines 4-8); no test references low_stock.
